Richards Bay Minerals.desc: A mineral sands mining and processing company on the coast of northern KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa, producing mainly ilmenite, rutile and zircon plus titanium slag and pig iron. Rio Tinto holds 74%, Blue Horizon (investors with the Mbonambi, Sokhulu, Mkhwanazi and Dube host communities) holds 24% and an employee trust the remainder; in 2019 it made 563,264 tonnes of slag and 141,645 tonnes of zircon and had 1,854 employees and 3,182 contractors.

sources.title: Richards Bay Minerals: Invested in South Africa
South Africa - operations

Rössing Uranium Ltd.desc: An open-pit uranium mining company at Arandis in Namibia's Erongo region, commissioned in 1976, which sells uranium oxide to nuclear power users. China National Uranium Corporation, part of China National Nuclear Corporation, became its majority shareholder in 2019; output passed 3,100 tonnes of uranium oxide in 2025, its highest since 2011.

sources.title: About us

SEPHOS SA (Tervalis group).desc: A phosphate mining company registered in Senegal as SEPHOS SENEGAL S.A., which mines calcium phosphate (phosphate de chaux) at Lam-Lam in the Thies region. A 2016 ministerial order assessing its mining royalty records sales of 2,098.58 tonnes in Senegal and exports of 233,903.88 tonnes for that year, on which it owed 161.57 million CFA francs at the 3% rate set by the 2003 Mining Code.

sources.title: Arrete fixant la redevance miniere due par la societe SEPHOS Senegal, exercice 2016
sources.publisher: Ministere de l'Industrie et des Mines, Senegal (vie-publique.sn)

sources.title: 2017-2018 Minerals Yearbook: Senegal

SEPHOS SA (Tervalis group).note: No source opened links SEPHOS to the Tervalis group or names its owners, so nothing is said about ownership. The USGS yearbook lists a phosphate producer at Lam Lam under the name Societe Senegalaise de Phosphates de Thies SA without ownership details, and whether that is the same company is not stated.

PT Vale Indonesia (formerly PT Inco).desc: An Indonesian nickel mining and smelting company, set up in 1968 and listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange since 1990 under the code INCO, producing on average about 75,000 tonnes of nickel in matte a year from laterite ore. Its own company page lists Vale Canada Limited at 43.79%, the Indonesian state mining holding MIND ID at 20% (from October 2020), Sumitomo Metal Mining at 15.03% and public investors at 21.18%, and a contract-of-work area of about 118,017 hectares across Sulawesi.

sources.title: About PT Vale Indonesia

Vale S.A..desc: A Brazilian mining company organised in 1943 with its head office in Rio de Janeiro, producing iron ore, iron ore pellets, nickel and copper, with platinum group metals, gold, silver and cobalt as by-products. Its shares trade on the Novo Mercado of Brazil's B3 exchange and as American depositary shares on the New York Stock Exchange under VALE; net operating revenue from continuing operations was US$41.8 billion in 2023.

sources.title: Form 20-F for the year ended December 31, 2023
sources.publisher: Vale S.A. / U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission

Wuxi Huaguang Electric Power Engineering.note: Searched in English and Chinese for 'Wuxi Huaguang Electric Power Engineering' / 无锡华光电力工程有限公司. The only page naming this exact company was a job-board listing (maukerja.my), which is marketing copy rather than a filing or register entry. The credible results all concern a different entity, Wuxi Huaguang Boiler Co / Wuxi Huaguang Environment & Energy Group (Shanghai Stock Exchange 600475); its 2024 disclosure on cninfo/dfcfw was opened and does not mention the company in the key. Left blank rather than describe that firm as if it were this one.

Vestas Wind Systems.desc: A Danish company that designs, makes and installs onshore and offshore wind turbines and sells service and maintenance for wind farms. Revenue was EUR 17.3 billion in 2024, with an order intake of 17 GW worth EUR 19 billion and a combined order backlog of EUR 68.4 billion.

sources.title: Vestas Annual report 2024 - progress in a challenging year

Sindh Engro Coal Mining Company (SECMC).desc: A Pakistani coal mining company that developed the country's first open-pit lignite mine, in Block II of the Thar desert in Sindh. Its majority shareholder is the government of Sindh, with Engro Energy, Thal Limited, Habib Bank, Hub Power and China Machinery Engineering Corporation as joint venture partners and Houlinhe Open Pit Coal Mine as a strategic investor; mine capacity has been raised from 3.8 to 7.6 million tonnes a year, and it had 222 staff at the end of 2023.

sources.title: Sindh Engro Coal Mining (SECMC)
Annual Report December 2023

Urbaser.desc: A waste and environmental services company founded in Madrid in 1990. It collects and treats household and industrial waste, cleans streets and manages water, with revenue of about EUR 2.3 billion in 2020 and more than 50,000 staff in 25 countries, mainly Spain, Chile, Argentina, France and the Nordic countries. The US buyout firm Platinum Equity bought it from China Tianying in October 2021 at an enterprise value of about EUR 3.5 billion.

sources.title: Platinum Equity Acquires Global Environmental Services Business Urbaser

Sinomine Resource Group.desc: A Chinese mining and mineral processing company listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange under code 002738. It mines lithium concentrate and refines battery-grade lithium salts, makes caesium and rubidium salts (including caesium formate for oil and gas drilling), and does mineral exploration; operating revenue was RMB 5.36 billion in 2024, down 10.8% on the year.

sources.title: 2024 Annual Report Summary (2024年年度报告摘要)
sources.publisher: Sinomine Resource Group Co., Ltd. / cninfo (Shenzhen Stock Exchange disclosure)

Sime Darby Plantation.desc: A Malaysian palm oil company listed on the Main Market of Bursa Malaysia since November 2017 under the code SIMEPLT, with Permodalan Nasional Berhad as controlling shareholder on 55.1% and the Employees Provident Fund on 15.2%. In 2022 it had 579,708 hectares planted within a land bank of 744,188 hectares, estates and mills in Malaysia, Indonesia, Papua New Guinea and the Solomon Islands, revenue of RM21.03 billion and 82,841 employees; it also refines palm oil into oils and fats, oleochemicals and biodiesel through Sime Darby Oils. It was renamed SD Guthrie Berhad in 2024.

sources.title: Annual Report 2022
Sime Darby Plantation returns to its roots, rebrands as SD Guthrie

PT Sumber Segara Primadaya (S2P).desc: An Indonesian independent power producer that owns the coal-fired Cilacap power station in Central Java. It is 51% owned by PT Sumberenergi Sakti Prima and 49% by the state generating company PT Pembangkit Jawa-Bali; its Cilacap expansion unit adds 1,000 MW under the government's 35,000 MW programme.

sources.title: Proyek 35.000 MW: Groundbreaking PLTU Cilacap 1.000 MW
sources.publisher: Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources, Indonesia (ESDM)

The Walt Disney Company.desc: A media and entertainment company incorporated in Delaware and based in Burbank, California, with shares on the New York Stock Exchange under DIS. It reports three business segments - Entertainment, Sports and Experiences - and had about 233,000 employees at the end of its 2024 financial year, roughly 171,000 of them in the United States.

sources.title: 2024 Annual Report (Form 10-K)

Ternium (Las Encinas).desc: Ternium is a steel producer incorporated in Luxembourg, selling to manufacturers and builders across the Americas, with American depositary shares on the New York Stock Exchange under TX; it shipped 15.6 million tonnes of steel on net sales of US$17.6 billion in 2024. Las Encinas is an iron ore mining company in Mexico, held 100% by its subsidiary Ternium Mexico.

sources.title: Ternium Announces Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2024 Results (Form 6-K)
sources.publisher: Ternium S.A. / U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission

sources.title: Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025
sources.publisher: Ternium S.A. / U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission

Procesadora Metalúrgica (Promel).desc: A small Chilean metals-processing firm at Arica that took in industrial residues from the European mining company Boliden from about 1984, intending to extract gold and silver from them. It gave up the processing soon afterwards and later went bankrupt.

sources.title: 20 mil toneladas de desechos tóxicos en el patio: la historia detrás del juicio que Arica perdió en Suecia

State Hydraulic Works (DSI).desc: Turkey's state water agency, the General Directorate of State Hydraulic Works, set up by Law No. 6200 of December 1953, which took effect in February 1954, and placed under the Ministry of Public Works. Its duties are flood and torrent protection, building irrigation systems and reclaiming swamps, generating hydroelectric power from its water schemes, approving and supervising town water and sewerage designs, and making rivers navigable.

sources.title: Law No. 6200 on the Establishment and Duties of the General Directorate of State Hydraulic Works
sources.publisher: Republic of Turkey / FAOLEX (FAO legal database)

Southern Peru Copper Corporation (Southe.desc: A copper mining company incorporated in Delaware in 1952, with shares on the New York and Lima stock exchanges under SCCO. Grupo Mexico owned 88.9% of its stock through its subsidiary Americas Mining Corporation at the end of 2024, when it had 16,133 employees and about 12,400 contractors. It runs the Toquepala and Cuajone open-pit mines and the Ilo smelter and refinery in Peru, and open-pit and underground mines, smelters and refineries in Mexico.

sources.title: Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024
sources.publisher: Southern Copper Corporation / U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission

Shell CAPSA.desc: Shell's Argentine oil company, descended from the Anglo Mexican Petroleum Products Co, which began importing fuel into Buenos Aires in 1914. Its Dock Sud refinery near Buenos Aires opened in May 1931 with a capacity of 1,000 tonnes of crude a day; it made petrol, diesel, aviation fuel, LPG, lubricants, asphalt and industrial chemicals such as solvents and polyols, and supplied more than 1,100 service stations by the early 2000s.

sources.title: Shell en la Argentina: 100 años
sources.publisher: Petrotecnia (Instituto Argentino del Petróleo y del Gas)

Scatec Solar (Scatec ASA).desc: A Norwegian renewable energy company based in Oslo and listed on the Oslo Stock Exchange under SCATC. It develops, builds, owns and operates solar, wind and hydropower plants, mostly in emerging markets, with 4.8 GW in operation and under construction reported for 2024.

sources.title: Scatec publishes Annual Integrated Report 2024
sources.publisher: Scatec ASA (via Inderes news release service)

Salini Impregilo.desc: An Italian infrastructure construction group, renamed Webuild on 4 May 2020 after taking over its compatriot Astaldi. At the time of the change the merged group reported an order backlog of EUR 42.5 billion and about 70,000 direct and indirect employees worldwide, rising to about 130,000 counting its supply chain.

sources.title: Salini Impregilo becomes Webuild: bigger, stronger and ready to serve the nation

Rhodia (Rhône-Poulenc, now Solvay).desc: A French chemicals maker whose products included surfactants and phosphorus chemicals, polyamide 6.6, silica and rare earth materials, and acetate tow. The Belgian chemicals group Solvay completed a friendly takeover of it on 16 September 2011; Rhodia had pro forma net sales of EUR 6.17 billion and 14,255 full-time equivalent staff at the end of 2011.

sources.title: Annual Report 2011

Van Oord.desc: A Dutch marine contractor based in Rotterdam, working in dredging, land and coastal infrastructure and offshore energy. It is family-owned and in its fifth generation of family leadership; revenue was EUR 2.9 billion in 2023 and it had 5,766 full-time staff at the end of that year.

sources.title: Van Oord - Annual accounts 2023: record high revenue
Van Oord in brief - Annual Report 2024

Suape Industrial Port Complex.desc: A Pernambuco state-owned port company that runs the Suape industrial and port complex south of Recife, which marked 47 years in November 2025. It is described as Brazil's sixth-largest public port and the country's leading handler of liquid bulk cargo, with 90 companies installed on the site and more than 30,000 direct and indirect jobs.

sources.title: Porto de Suape faz 47 anos e anuncia R$ 1,3 bilhão em infraestrutura para os próximos três anos

RP Global.desc: A renewable energy developer, owner and operator with offices in Vienna and Madrid, building small hydro, wind, solar and storage plants ranging from 3 MW to 500 MW, and reporting a development pipeline of about 16 GW. In October 2024 the French asset manager Mirova agreed to invest up to EUR 480 million in equity and mezzanine bonds for a significant minority shareholding.

sources.title: Schoenherr advises RP Global on Mirova's EUR 480m investment
RP Global Austria GmbH - developer, investor and operator of hydro, PV and wind projects

Sociedad Austral de Electricidad (SAESA).desc: A Chilean electricity distribution, transmission and generation group with its head office in Osorno, supplying southern Chile. In 2008 it served about 2.6 million people, 16% of the country's population, and owned 135 MW of wind, hydro and thermal generation and 950 km of transmission lines. Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan and Morgan Stanley Infrastructure bought it from the US utility Public Service Enterprise Group in July 2008 for US$887 million, each taking 50%.

sources.title: Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan and Morgan Stanley Infrastructure complete acquisition of SAESA Group

Sempra Energy.desc: A utility holding company based in San Diego, California, with shares on the New York Stock Exchange. Its regulated utilities are San Diego Gas & Electric, Southern California Gas Company and the Texas network Oncor Electric Delivery, and it holds a part interest in Sempra Infrastructure Partners, which exports liquefied natural gas and runs the Energía Costa Azul LNG terminal in Baja California, Mexico. It employs about 20,000 people, serves some 40 million consumers and had more than $110 billion of consolidated assets at the end of 2025.

sources.title: Our business / About us

Sumitomo Corporation.desc: A Japanese general trading and investment company established in 1919, organised into ten business groups covering steel, automotive, transport and construction systems, urban development, communications, digital, consumer goods, mineral resources, chemicals and energy. It has 82,488 group employees, 519 group companies and 123 offices in 62 countries and regions, and reported net income of 600.3 billion yen for the 2024 financial year.

sources.title: At a Glance

Salazar Resources.desc: A mineral exploration company that searches for copper and gold in Ecuador, quoted under SRL on the TSX Venture Exchange, SRLZF on the OTCQB and CCG in Frankfurt. It holds a wholly owned pipeline of exploration projects plus carried interests of 25% in Curipamba and 20% each in Pijili and Santiago, and co-founded The Salazar Foundation with the Salazar family.

sources.title: Salazar Welcomes New Partner Silvercorp Metals

Silvercorp Metals.desc: A Canadian mining company listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange and NYSE American under SVM, producing silver, gold, lead and zinc from several mines in the Ying mining district of Henan province and the GC mine in Guangdong province, China. Revenue was US$298.9 million and silver output about 6.95 million ounces in the year to 31 March 2025. It gained a 75% interest in Ecuador's El Domo copper-gold project and 98.7% of the Condor gold project when it acquired Adventus Mining Corporation on 31 July 2024.

sources.title: Management's Discussion and Analysis, fiscal year ended March 31, 2025

Umeme (Eskom 44%, Globeleq 56% at start).desc: A Ugandan electricity distribution company, listed on the Uganda Securities Exchange and cross-listed on the Nairobi Securities Exchange, which ran Uganda's main distribution network from 2005 until 31 March 2025. Over that period connections grew from about 290,000 to roughly 2.2 million and the network to more than 42,000 km. After handing the network to the state company UEDCL its staff fell from 2,409 to 18, it reported a 2025 loss of 223.6 billion Ugandan shillings and it says it has no operating business.

sources.title: After 20 years in Uganda, Umeme is now eyeing Sierra Leone

Vale Coal Colombia / CNR III.note: No source opened names either 'Vale Coal Colombia' or 'CNR III'. What could be verified concerns the group they sat in: Vale bought the Colombian coal assets in 2008 for US$308m and agreed in 2012 to sell the El Hatillo mine, the Cerro Largo deposit, Sociedad Portuaria Rio Cordoba and 8.43% of the FENOCO railway to Goldman Sachs-controlled Colombian Natural Resources (nsenergybusiness.com, 2012); Murray Energy then bought Colombian Natural Resources with the La Francia and El Hatillo mines and over 184 million short tons of reserves (worldcoal.com, 2015). Left blank rather than present the parent or the later owner as the company in the key.

Samtan.desc: A South Korean resource and energy company active in coal. In 2011 it held 49% of PT Kideco Jaya Agung, a coal miner in East Kalimantan, Indonesia, and offered coal marketing agency services; in December 2017 it sold most of that holding to Indika Energy, keeping 9%.

sources.title: Samtan seeks Indonesia new coal mine acquisition
Indika completes acquisition of Kideco

Power Construction Corporation of China.desc: A Chinese state-owned engineering and construction group formed in September 2011 and based in Beijing. It plans, surveys, designs and builds hydropower, thermal power, renewable energy and other infrastructure, and installs and makes electrical and mechanical equipment, with further business in property, investment and finance. Fortune's Global 500 profile ranks it 104th, with revenues of about US$102 billion and 179,815 employees, and records it as at least 50% government-owned.

sources.title: PowerChina - Fortune Global 500
The Power Construction Corporation of China
sources.publisher: Belt and Road Portal (yidaiyilu.gov.cn), sourced from SASAC

Xiamen Xiangyu Co..desc: A Chinese commodity supply-chain services company listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange under code 600057. It buys raw materials and distributes products for manufacturers and provides logistics, supply chain finance and information services. Its controlling shareholder is Xiamen Xiangyu Group Co., Ltd, which held about 51.3% at the end of 2024; operating revenue that year was RMB 366.67 billion, down 20.1%, with 7,929 staff.

sources.title: 2024 Annual Report (2024年年度报告)
sources.publisher: Xiamen Xiangyu Co., Ltd. (Shanghai Stock Exchange disclosure)

Shell (Shell Brasil).desc: Shell Brasil Petroleo Ltda is Shell plc's oil and gas company in Brazil and the country's second-largest oil producer after Petrobras, with output of 420,000 to 450,000 barrels a day in 2025, up from about 400,000 a day a year earlier. Its production comes mainly from pre-salt fields in the Santos Basin, including Mero, which it works with Petrobras.

sources.title: Apos recorde, Shell mira manter producao entre 420-450 mil barris/dia no Brasil este ano
Shell invests in the Gato do Mato project in Brazil's pre-salt

Red Back Mining.desc: A Canadian gold mining company whose shares traded on the Toronto Stock Exchange, with the Tasiast mine in Mauritania among its assets. Kinross Gold completed its takeover on 17 September 2010, paying 1.778 Kinross shares and 0.11 of a warrant for each Red Back share, and the shares were delisted on 21 September 2010.

sources.title: Kinross Gold Corporation, Form 6-K (2010): completion of the Red Back Mining acquisition
sources.publisher: Kinross Gold Corporation / U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission

Radio Corporation of America (RCA).desc: An American electronics and broadcasting company founded in 1919 by General Electric to run an American-owned radio business, taking over the assets of the Marconi Wireless Telegraph Company of America. It helped form the NBC broadcasting network in 1926, bought the Victor Talking Machine Company in 1929, ran RCA Laboratories at Princeton, New Jersey from 1941, and developed the colour television system adopted as the United States standard in 1953. It also made computers until 1971 and moved into car rental, frozen food and publishing. General Electric took it over in 1986, then broke it up and sold the parts.

sources.title: Radio Corporation of America

Thomson Consumer Electronics / Technicol.desc: A French electronics and media company based at Issy-les-Moulineaux, formed in 1966 from the merger of Compagnie Francaise Thomson-Houston and Hotchkiss-Brandt, nationalised in 1982 and reorganised as the holding company Thomson S.A. in 1983. In 1987 it bought General Electric's consumer electronics division, which included RCA; that arm was named Thomson Consumer Electronics in 1988 and Thomson Multimedia in 1995, the company was floated in 1999 and took the name Technicolor in 2010. It made televisions, DVD players and video equipment and became the world's largest maker of disc media such as DVDs and CDs.

sources.title: Technicolor SA

Xinyi Glass Holdings.desc: A glass maker incorporated in the Cayman Islands and listed on the main board of the Hong Kong Stock Exchange under code 00868. In 2024 float glass was 57.8% of its sales, automobile glass 28.3% and architectural glass 13.9%; revenue was RMB 22.32 billion, net profit RMB 3.37 billion and staff 16,485. It has plants across mainland China and at Malacca in Malaysia, and is building a float and automotive glass complex at Gresik, Indonesia.

sources.title: Annual Results Announcement for the year ended 31 December 2024

PT Makmur Elok Graha.desc: An Indonesian property development company, a subsidiary of the Artha Graha group owned by the businessman Tomy Winata. Its cooperation agreement over Rempang dates from 2004 and runs for 30 years, renewable for another 30 and then 20 more, at rent of about Rp26,000 per square metre, a total the newspaper put at Rp1.2 trillion.

sources.title: Perusahaan Tomy Winata Sewa Rempang Rp26.000 per Meter Selama 30 Tahun

Sino-Metals Leach Zambia.desc: A copper producer registered in 2004 at Kalulushi in Zambia's Copperbelt, inside the Zambia-China Economic and Trade Cooperation Zone. It is owned by the Chinese state-owned China Nonferrous Metal Mining Group (55%), Hong Kong Zhongfei Mining Investment (30%) and NFC Africa Mining (15%), has yearly capacity of 8,000 tonnes of copper cathode and 4,000 tonnes of copper concentrate, and employs 426 Zambian and Chinese staff.

sources.title: Sino-Metals' jobs, investments create goodwill between China and Zambia
Sino-Metal Leach (project record)
sources.publisher: China Global South Project, Africa Mining database

Shell Nigeria Exploration and Production.desc: Shell's deep-water oil and gas producer in the Gulf of Guinea, wholly owned by Shell plc and one of the four Shell companies in Nigeria. It holds 55% of OML 118 and OML 135, both Shell-operated, and 43.75% of the Esso-operated OML 133; its OPL 245 licence expired in 2021. Shell's two Nigerian producers together put out 367,683 barrels of oil equivalent a day in 2022, and SNEPCo paid US$907 million in Nigerian corporate taxes and royalties that year.

sources.title: Shell Nigeria Briefing Notes 2022
sources.publisher: The Shell Petroleum Development Company of Nigeria

Shell plc.desc: An oil and gas company incorporated in England and Wales with its principal office at Shell Centre in London, employing about 96,000 people in more than 70 countries. Its businesses are integrated gas and LNG, upstream oil and gas, fuels and lubricants marketing with the Shell service station network, refining and chemicals, and power, hydrogen and carbon capture. Income for 2024 was US$16.5 billion on operating cash flow of US$54.7 billion, and it has American depositary shares and trades on Euronext Amsterdam and in London.

sources.title: Annual Report and Accounts 2024 (Form 6-K)
sources.publisher: Shell plc / U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission

TVI Pacific Inc..desc: A publicly traded Canadian resource company that takes and holds interests in Asia-Pacific mining projects rather than running them itself. Its main asset is a 30.66% interest in TVI Resource Development (Phils.) Inc., a former wholly owned subsidiary whose control it gave up in December 2013; TVIRD's projects include the Balabag gold-silver mine, the Siana gold mine, the Mabilo copper-gold project and the Agata nickel-iron mine, whose operations ended in 2023.

sources.title: History and Company Overview

Plantations du Haut Penja (PHP).desc: A banana grower and exporter in Cameroon, the local subsidiary of the French group Compagnie Fruitiere of Marseille. It is the country's largest banana exporter: it shipped 42,977 tonnes in the first quarter of 2023, 80.3% of Cameroon's exports in that quarter, down from an 85.3% share a year earlier.

sources.title: Cameroon: Plantations du Haut Penja still leads banana market in Q1 2023

SOCO International plc.desc: An oil and gas exploration and production company headquartered in London and listed on the London Stock Exchange, which changed its registered name to Pharos Energy plc on 16 October 2019. At that point it held a 100% working interest in the El Fayum oil concession in Egypt's Western Desert, worked through a 50/50 joint venture with the Egyptian General Petroleum Corporation, and interests in the Te Giac Trang and Ca Ngu Vang fields and Blocks 125 and 126 offshore Vietnam.

sources.title: Proposed change to registered name to Pharos Energy plc gains shareholder approval

Tampieri Financial Group.desc: An Italian business group that buys raw grains to supply an edible oil factory in Italy, reported in 2013 to be planning a 15 million euro investment in Senegal over five years.

sources.title: Senegal's shady farmland agreement

Tampieri Financial Group.note: The only description of the group itself that could be opened is Al Jazeera's, which says little beyond the edible oil factory. A Creditsafe business-register entry for a differently named company, Tampieri S.p.A. of Via Granarolo, Faenza (joint-stock, incorporated 2001, 'manufacture of vegetable oils other than olive oil'), was opened but is not stated to be the same entity, so it is not used here.

Senhuile SA.desc: A Senegalese farming company, first incorporated as Senethanol, which Al Jazeera reported in 2013 as 51% owned by Italy's Tampieri Financial Group and 49% by Senethanol SA, itself 75% owned by Agro Bioethanol Int LLC of New York (registered 2009) and 25% by unnamed Senegalese investors. Set up in 2010 to grow sweet potato for bioethanol for Europe, it switched to sunflower seed for export to Italy on a 20,000-hectare lease, and production had been discontinued by the time of reporting.

sources.title: Senegal's shady farmland agreement
Surrendering Our Future: Senhuile-Senethanol Plantation Destroys Local Communities and Jeopardizes Environment

Stora Enso.desc: A forest products company that makes packaging materials and packaging solutions, biomaterials and wood products for construction, and is one of the largest private forest owners in the world. Sales were about EUR 9.0 billion in 2024 and it had roughly 19,000 employees.

sources.title: Stora Enso reports 4Q, full year 2024 results

Stora Enso.note: No source opened gives the company's stock exchange listing or head office, so neither is stated.

Wildlife Alliance.desc: A conservation organisation registered as a 501(c)(3) non-profit in New York with its headquarters in Phnom Penh, Cambodia. It was founded in 1995 as the Global Survival Network and renamed Wildlife Alliance in 2006, and runs forest protection, wildlife rescue, reforestation, community agriculture and ecotourism work, mainly in Cambodia's Southern Cardamom Mountains, with other projects in Thailand, Myanmar, the Russian Far East, India and Ecuador. It reported revenue of US$9.23 million against expenses of US$11.76 million for the year to December 2024.
